clue.text: Cope before getting resistance from trainer

parts.note: to cope with something is to handle it
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone copes with things before meeting resistance from their coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog or animal handler is the person who trains and controls the animal.

clue.text: Indifference over a continental business

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: un is the French word for a, a continental's article
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: Apathy shown about some European company.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of concern is a state of not caring, so it is a synonym for apathy.

clue.text: After a time I get in the drink in the entrance hall

indicators.note: the letter I is to get into the drink, so it goes inside that word

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: After a while I start drinking in the lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a time' looks like a phrase meaning later, but it supplies A and T, which open the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is the central hall or court at the entrance of a building, a lobby.

clue.text: Hooter not heard in the daytime?

definitions.text: Hooter not heard in the daytime?

parts.words: Hooter not heard in the daytime?
parts.note: a hooter is literally an owl, silent by day; the phrase also names a person who stays up late

explanation.surface: A horn or siren that is silent during the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls hoot at dark hours, and the term is used for someone who is most active late in the evening.

clue.text: There's not an item to be gained after it, so it is said

definitions.text: There's not an item to be gained after it, so it is said

parts.words: There's not an item to be gained after it, so it is said
parts.note: the proverb runs on with 'nothing gained', so not a thing is won after these words

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing will be won afterwards, as the saying goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that if you risk nothing you gain nothing; the first half is what precedes 'nothing gained'.

clue.text: Spoon possibly found at nineteenth hole

definitions.meaning: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf stick, so an example of one
the nineteenth hole is the bar in a golf clubhouse, so the club itself

explanation.surface: A piece of cutlery turns up in the bar after a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon was a type of wooden golf stick; the nineteenth hole is golfers' slang for the bar at their clubhouse.

clue.text: Play monotonously, that's almost the spirit

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Strumming away tediously, someone says that it is almost the right attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrum is to strum a guitar idly or drum fingers in a dull repetitive way.

clue.text: Attractive — only partly successful?

definitions.meaning: read as two words it suggests you ... battles but not all

explanation.surface: Something appealing that only partly comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming; split, it recalls the saying 'you win some, you lose some' for mixed success.

clue.text: Lady in sports car had the bird

indicators.note: the lady's name sits inside the car's letters

parts.note: GT (gran turismo) is a common label for a sports car
Anne is a woman's name, the lady here

explanation.surface: A woman in a sports car got jeered at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had the bird' suggests being booed off stage; only 'bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large white seabird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Rattle on about being broad-minded

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chatters on about being liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal person accepts views unlike their own, which is what open-minded acceptance means.

clue.text: Simon had suffered rebuke

indicators.note: suffered suggests the letters have been knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Simon was told off after he had gone through a bad time.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to reprimand or scold someone, a synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Land for everyone

definitions.meaning: a piece of open public ground in a village
shared by all, belonging to everybody

explanation.definitionFit: A village green open to all is called by this name, and the adjective means shared by all people.

clue.text: Female with churchman, trusty supporter

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, used for a woman
CH is the abbreviation for church, followed by the word man

explanation.surface: A woman with a clergyman, his loyal helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churchman' reads as a cleric, but splits as CH (church) plus MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a faithful follower or right-hand man, often of a villain.

clue.text: Informed guide leader first who complained

indicators.note: first says this letter goes at the front
the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: rumbled is British slang for found out, discovered, having become informed of a secret

explanation.surface: Someone tipped off guided the group leader first, then moaned.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to moan or grouse, so the past tense matches whined.

clue.text: As much beer as can be put in one container?

definitions.text: As much beer as can be put in one container?

parts.words: As much beer as can be put in one container?
parts.note: the amount held by a single cask, read literally

explanation.surface: Asking how much ale fits into one vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask holds a fixed quantity; this word names exactly that amount.

clue.text: Gang placed two articles back to back in handkerchief

parts.note: a band is a group or gang of people
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the two articles stand back to back, so the second one is turned round

parts.note: the second of the two articles, also an

explanation.surface: A gang put two items one against the other inside a kerchief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to back' turns the second AN into NA, so the two articles meet at their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large coloured handkerchief worn round the head or neck.

clue.text: It's hard to sell

parts.note: reads as a tricky product, but means goods of a hard metal offered for sale

explanation.surface: Something that is difficult to find buyers for.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware such as pots and tools made of a tough metal is sold by ironmongers.

clue.text: Knock on left side evokes sympathy

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A knock on the left side provokes sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, understanding relationship, a sense of mutual sympathy.

clue.text: Yet Lew's performing in a melodious way

indicators.note: the letters are put on show in a new order, as if acting

parts.note: the name with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Still, Lew sings beautifully when on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in a pleasant, tuneful manner is what this adverb describes.

clue.text: Colour of hazel when fully developed!

definitions.text: Colour of hazel when fully developed!

parts.words: Colour of hazel when fully developed!
parts.note: the hazel tree's fruit turns this shade once ripe

explanation.surface: Describing the shade of a hazel tree at maturity.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripe hazelnut has a warm reddish-tan shade, and the colour is named after it.

clue.text: Thanks poet for the coat

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: Thanking a poet for a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic or herald's short coat bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Voluntarily parted with fancy drapes

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone willingly gave away some ornate curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare something is to give it up willingly, as in sparing a moment.

clue.text: Bird welcome in the navy

indicators.note: the greeting goes inside the navy's letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A bird is received in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: One in Paris willingly be included despite lack of faith

indicators.note: be is to be included within the other letters

parts.note: un is French for one
lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly

explanation.surface: A Parisian is keen to join in despite having no faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelief is absence of religious belief, the lack of trust in a creed.

clue.text: Our vines producing something worth keeping

indicators.note: producing means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Our vineyard turning out a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a memento kept to remind you of a place or event.

clue.text: Do not start to worry about money

indicators.note: the word for worry loses its first letter

parts.note: trouble means bother or worry

explanation.surface: Don't begin fretting about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency unit of Russia.

clue.text: Usual colours

definitions.meaning: a regimental flag carried into battle

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or typical; a standard is also a military flag, like regimental colours.
